Both original and regularized certificates have this side; issue SHA-256 values a1a3b6e7c2ce4d7de79efc2e07fc0bf53616dc44b732a2849b4dc4d8f7e2c4cc and ab3c0b93aa205a907da5387cc119df11164c0a6d63b49b81332d7ce77910a897.

The author reports both standalone stdlib exact checkers accept both certificates. They share authorship and certificate format but use separating axes and polygon intersections, respectively. Acquisition retains their source and does not execute them or infer independent outside authorship.

The issue credits Daniil Ostashev's T-149 as the starting packing, then a chain of 18 basin-explorer moves. It reports a different local minimum, KKT/second-order and corner-corner MILP diagnostics at 80 digits, and a 17-angle-group regularized view; these are numerical evidence, not interval proofs or a claim of global optimality. Comparison files and numerical inputs are retained as source assertions.
